Refresh.Title: Automatic refresh
Refresh.Policy: Automatic reads pause in background. Inventory refreshes share a cached snapshot.

Access.Description: The host operational policy does not allow this workspace.

Map.Finding: Ownership is evaluated at each source’s observation time. A retained expired record does not establish whether its worker is running.
Map.Title: Ownership map
Map.Description: Select a responsibility to inspect its evidence
Map.More: View {0} more in the records below

Evidence.Stale: A refresh failed. Last successful evidence keeps its original source time; unavailable authorities are shown separately.
Evidence.Retry: Retry the read. No conclusion about ownership can be made from a failed query.
Evidence.UnconfiguredDescription: Register the lease stores and permitted scope/prefix bindings in the host to inspect them here.
Evidence.ClaimsTitle: A role lease is not a message or job claim
Evidence.ClaimsDescription: Job execution and Outbox delivery claims stay with their business records. This view covers shared coordination responsibilities.
Evidence.EmptyDescription: The configured queries returned no records. Absence does not prove that a responsibility was never acquired.
Evidence.Retention: SQL can retain expired rows. Expired Redis keys disappear from the inventory.
Evidence.CaptureNote: Validity is measured at each authority’s observation. These values are snapshots, not live countdowns.
Evidence.Title: Lease evidence
Evidence.ExactFailed: The exact read failed. Any earlier evidence retains its original observation time.
Evidence.ExactHint: An exact lookup reads one resource without enumerating the inventory.
Evidence.Name: Resource name
Evidence.TimelineNote: These points describe one retained grant. Previous holders and renewal history are not recorded here.
Evidence.Missing: No retained observation for this resource
Evidence.MissingDescription: The record may have expired, been revoked, or been removed. This inventory is not ownership history.

Inventory.Title: Lease records
Inventory.Description: Find a responsibility, then inspect its exact resource.
Inventory.NoMatchDescription: Try another authority or remove the search and evidence filters.

Meaning.Sql: A relational authority can support durable coordination. Transactional protection depends on the consumer validating its grant within the protected transaction.
Meaning.Redis: Redis coordinates repeatable background work. Asynchronous failover may lose an acknowledged grant, so this authority is advisory.
Meaning.InMemory: This source coordinates only within its current process. Independent replicas do not share these grants.
Meaning.Custom: The host supplied this authority. Its implementation defines expiry, consistency and transaction guarantees.

Admin.Title: Administration
Admin.Warning: Revocation does not immediately stop a worker. A successor may acquire while previous work is still active.
Admin.Unavailable: This binding does not expose administrative revocation.
Admin.ConfirmTitle: Revoke the current lease for this resource?
Admin.ConfirmDescription: This removes whichever grant exists when the action executes. It may belong to a different holder than the one shown.
Admin.Acknowledge: I understand that work may overlap.
Admin.Failed: Revocation could not be confirmed. Refresh the evidence before deciding whether to retry.

Locks.PreviewNote: Changes this view, not the service configuration.
Locks.CompareNote: One calling pattern; different coordination and loss guarantees.
Locks.Unknown: This provider is not in the example
Locks.UnknownNote: The default mechanism is shown. Choose one of the providers below to continue.
Locks.AcquireNote: No handle means no protected work.
Locks.WorkNote: Pass cancellation into the work and await its completion.
Locks.ReleaseNote: Await handle disposal when leaving the ownership scope.
Locks.DiagramNote: This is a calling sequence, not live execution, ownership or timing evidence.
Locks.ContractNote: This view compares provider contracts. No lock runtime data from this service is connected.
Locks.InventoryNote: Holders, queue depth and wait times cannot be listed from this API.
Locks.RevokeNote: The caller that acquired the handle owns its release.
Locks.BoundaryNote: Lock loss or cancellation does not undo a sent request. Keep transaction and concurrency checks on database writes.
Locks.RoleLinkNote: Scheduler roles, Outbox maintenance and discovery leadership.

InProcess.Label: Within one process
InProcess.Finding: For serial access to resources shared within one process. Other replicas have their own locks and do not join this coordination.
InProcess.LossNote: Disposing the handle releases the local semaphore. There is no loss notification; still observe caller cancellation.
InProcess.Expiry: Released by handle disposal; no independent expiry
InProcess.Signal: Not observed; token is not cancelable

Medallion.Label: Native coordination
Medallion.Finding: For coordination across replicas with lock-loss observation. The chosen native backend determines expiry and renewal.
Medallion.LossTitle: On lock loss, stop and drain the work
Medallion.LossNote: Forwards the native HandleLostToken. Reading it may start backend monitoring; the work must respond to cancellation.
Medallion.Expiry: Expiry and renewal follow native provider options
Medallion.Signal: Native handle signal; capability depends on the backend

Dapr.Label: A fixed lifetime
Dapr.Context: Same App ID · Same lock store
Dapr.Finding: For a Dapr lock component and work bounded by a known lifetime. This adapter neither renews the lock nor observes its loss.
Dapr.LossTitle: Expiry does not stop the work
Dapr.LossNote: Give the work a shorter deadline. No loss notification is not proof of ownership; keep work within the known validity window.
Dapr.WorkHint: Work must finish before the lock expires
Dapr.Expiry: Fixed lease; Monica's adapter does not renew it
Dapr.Signal: Not observed; token is not cancelable
